messages:
ada: Heads up — seeing NaNs in prod after enabling fp8 + paged FlashAttention (paged_flash_v2). Appears during long-context requests (6k-8k). Logs point to softmax overflow inside attention kernel. Anyone else seen this?

matt: Can you paste a small log / repro? rough idea: is this only with kv-cache enabled or also full-attn?

ada: kv-cache enabled. snippet from runtime log:
```
attention_kernel.cu:line 412: softmax overflow, max_score=1147.3, exp(max_score) -> inf
stack: flash_attention::paged::compute_scores
```
This is with fp8 storage + fp16 compute path on A100s.

sophia: Interesting — our kernel selector switches to paged_flash_v2 when avg_seq>2048 and kv_hit_ratio>0.7. Paged uses tiled accumulation with minimal accumulator precision to save bandwidth. If accumulator stays fp16 or fp8, large logits can overflow.

ryan: I reproduced locally with a synthetic workload (batch of 16, seq 6144, dim=4096) using our paged kernel + fp8 weights. Repro command:
```bash
PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=garbage ./runtests --kernel paged_flash_v2 --dtype fp8 --batch 16 --seq 6144 --dim 4096
```
Got NaNs within first few tokens.

linda: Also flag: our batching heuristic will merge short requests into a single GPU batch, which can push the effective sequence length higher for the kernel and trigger the paged path. So sometimes this happens only when load patterns cause coalescing.

matt: Quick mitigation options:
- implement stable softmax (log-sum-exp) inside the kernel (safe but needs extra pass or reduce op)
- use bf16 accumulators for the reduction (wider dynamic range)
- clamp logits before exp (cheap but approximate; need to choose clamp threshold)
- fallback to fused_flash (which uses higher precision accumulator) when fp8 is enabled

sophia: Agreed. Fallback to fused_flash for fp8 would be fastest stopgap. Long term we should add a jitter-free stable softmax in paged kernels or cast reduction to bf16. Also consider detecting pathological score magnitude and trigger fallback at runtime.

ryan: Did quick perf microbench: (measured tokens/sec on A100, same model config)
- fused_flash (fp16): 100k tokens/s
- paged_flash_v2 (fp16): 118k tokens/s (+18%)
- paged_flash_v2 (fp8 weights, fp16 accum): NaN case -> invalid
- paged_flash_v2 (fp8 + clamp logits at [-30,30]): 114k tokens/s (+14%), no NaNs
- paged_flash_v2 (fp8 + bf16 accum): 112k tokens/s (+12%), stable
So clamp or bf16 accumulator both work; clamp is slightly faster.

ada: Perf regression from clamp is ~3-6% vs ideal paged fp8, but beats outage. We should prioritize correctness first.

matt: For correctness we should add two things: kernel-side check to detect exp overflow risk (e.g., if max_score>80) and fallback to safer kernel; and a canary rollout of the fallback path. Add a unit test that synthesizes large logits to catch regressions.

perf-bot: Canary deploy triggered: rollout/attn-fp8-fallback -> env=staging at 1769990420 by matt :rocket:

ada: Plan:
- sophia: add runtime selector gate -> if dtype==fp8 && paged_flash_v2 && max_score>threshold -> fallback to fused_flash (or bf16-accum variant)
- ryan: add perf microbench harness & run nightly so we can track perf delta
- matt: add unit/regression test + canary
Target: small patch + canary in 48h, wider rollout after green.

sophia: I'll open a draft PR for selector changes and a minimal patch to detect huge logits. Will include comments about long-term stable-softmax refactor.

ryan: I'll add perf-pipeline job to compare tokens/sec and tail-latency across kernels; also lock a perf regression alert at >7% throughput drop.

linda: Also let's add a change to batching heuristics: cap merged effective seq length for kernel choice evaluation (so coalescing doesn't accidentally flip to paged). I'll file a tiny follow-up.

matt: Good. One more note — we should add an eval with representative prompts that exercise long-context and kv hits; tie regression alerts to eval metric failures.

ada: Thanks all. I'll monitor staging after canary and ping if any anomalies. :thumbsup:

sophia: PR: https://git.internal/redwood/infra/pulls/1187 (draft)

ryan: Perf run scheduled: https://perf.internal/runs/attn-fp8-fallback/1770

matt: Assigning owners in JIRA: RW-1234 (fp8 kernel fallback), RW-1235 (perf bench), RW-1236 (batching cap).

ada: Closing loop: once we confirm no NaNs and perf within thresholds, we can enable fp8+paged in Dedicated.

linda: ack :heavy_check_mark:

matt: Thanks — nice find ada.
